name: fig4-cell-cycle
title: Fig 4 — Emergent, unregulated control of cell-cycle duration
question:
Does the viva-Mgen replication submodel reproduce Fig 4's central finding —
that M. genitalium's cell-cycle duration is controlled *emergently*, without a
dedicated genetic regulator, through the coupling of replication initiation and
a dNTP surplus that it builds up?
hypothesis:
If DnaA accumulates stochastically to trigger initiation while dNTPs
accumulate (unconsumed) during that same initiation phase, then across single
cells (1) more birth DnaA shortens initiation (Fig 4C), (2) a larger dNTP pool
at replication start shortens replication (Fig 4D), and (3) initiation and
replication durations are inversely correlated (Fig 4E) — a longer initiation
buys a bigger dNTP surplus that speeds replication, buffering total cycle length.
objective:
Simulate a population of ~128 single cells with random birth DnaA and dNTP
levels by stepping the ReplicationReproductionProcess directly, recover the
three Fig 4 single-cell correlations, and render a representative single-cell
dynamics trajectory through the fig4_cell_cycle composite.
description:
REDUCED MECHANISM, GENUINE DYNAMICS. This is a clean-room reproduction of the
emergent cell-cycle regulation Karr 2012 uncovered, not the full
replisome/Okazaki-fragment machinery of the original Replication submodel. The
mechanism is genuine: a dNTP-buffered three-phase cycle (initiation ->
replication -> done) in which DnaA accumulates stochastically to a threshold to
fire initiation, dNTPs accumulate unconsumed during initiation, and the
resulting surplus sets the speed of the deterministic, dNTP-limited replication
phase. No gene explicitly regulates cycle length; the buffering is emergent
from that coupling. Achieved (committed production run, 128/128 cells
completing): r(initiation, replication) = -0.930 (Fig 4E),
r(dNTP-at-start, replication) = -0.951 (Fig 4D),
r(initial DnaA, initiation) = -0.743 (Fig 4C).

conclusion:
viva-Mgen reproduces Fig 4's emergent cell-cycle regulation with a reduced but
mechanistically genuine dNTP-buffered replication model. Across 128 single
cells (all completing), the three signature correlations are clearly negative:
more birth DnaA shortens initiation (r = -0.743, Fig 4C), a larger starting
dNTP pool shortens replication (r = -0.951, Fig 4D), and initiation and
replication durations are inversely related (r = -0.930, Fig 4E) — the
self-buffering of total cycle length that arises without any dedicated genetic
regulator.
